pullRequests.title: Fix SABR subtitle loading for external caption files
pullRequests.head: 7f2616bebf3a94ac463612ea9d98ff41971f345b
pullRequests.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #6180.

This change corrects a subtitle loading failure during SABR playback.

## Cause

YouTube supplies these subtitles as separate text files.
The unmodified SABR loader sends these files to `ContainerMediaChunk`.
Text representations have no `ChunkExtractorWrapper`.
The loader calls `init()` on the null extractor and causes `Unexpected NullPointerException`.
Automatic retries can select DASH, which can make the failure difficult to reproduce.

## Changes

* Load external subtitle files with HTTP GET and `SingleSampleMediaChunk`.
* Include the visitor cookie in subtitle requests when available.
* Keep the original subtitle timestamps during playback and seek operations.
* End the subtitle stream after one file, including when the video duration is unknown.
* Keep subtitle selections separate from SABR requests for audio and video.
* Do not change the SABR media network when a subtitle request fails.

Audio and video keep the SABR request path.
The change also adds regression tests and updates the module documentation.

## Verification

All 20 SABR tests pass with JDK 11.
The change adds 14 regression tests.
Six of these tests fail with the unmodified code and pass with this change.
The tests cover WebVTT, TTML, subtitle data, timestamps, cookies, stream completion, network errors, and audio and video requests.

Run these commands from the repository root:

```sh
export JAVA_HOME=/path/to/jdk-11
bash ./gradlew :exoplayer-library-sabr:testStstableDebugUnitTest :smarttubetv:assembleStstableDebug
```

Manual checks used an Android TV 14 ARM64 emulator.
Subtitles appeared during playback, after an app restart, and after forward and backward seeks.
The fixed build produced no matching subtitle exception.
The checks do not cover physical Fire TV hardware.

## Reproduction

Use the [example video from the issue](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F4U-HfdTGG8).

1. Install the unmodified build from commit `a6d8d8153`.
2. Open the example video.
3. Select English under **Subtitles (autogenerated)**.
4. Close the app.
5. Start the app with the same video and subtitles enabled.
6. Check the application log for `Unexpected NullPointerException`.
7. Install the fixed build without deleting the app data.
8. Repeat steps 2 through 5.
9. Make sure the subtitles appear and playback continues.

The failure requires SABR playback.
Check the application log for `Loading video in sabr format...`.

## Screenshots

Both images show video `F4U-HfdTGG8` on the same emulator with autogenerated English subtitles selected.
The screenshots are on a separate branch in the fork, outside the code diff.

### Before the change

The unmodified build starts loading again after the subtitle exception.
The application log records `Unexpected NullPointerException` at `ContainerMediaChunk.java:123`.

![Before: the same video returns to loading with subtitles selected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yasoob/SmartTube/03af6b104c87329e7bbaa39a97b60659612b3bcb/smarttube-6180-before.png)

### After the change

The fixed build plays the same video and displays the subtitles after an app restart.

![After: the same video plays with visible English subtitles](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yasoob/SmartTube/03af6b104c87329e7bbaa39a97b60659612b3bcb/smarttube-6180-after.png)

pullRequests.title: subtitles: remember category rework
pullRequests.head: ed8a6ffe583fb188fd837002a00795200c024e93
pullRequests.body:
Hi,
I needed a way to enable subtitles for all channel regardless of the channel watched, and since I couldn't find a way in the settings I added it.
I replaced the "Remember enabled subtitles per each channel" switch with a new category called "Remember enabled subtitles" with the following options: "Do not remember", "Remember for each channel", "Remember globally". The logic for the first two options should be the same as before, but the new third option ignores the enabled subtitles channels and shows the subtitles at all times.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cfcfeaf7-b311-4007-8c15-1cfd014ece32)
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1dbb81f9-e736-4ac0-9b19-21a93c6d34de)

It should be almost ready to merge, but there's a couple things that should be kept in mind:
- the category ID in AppDialogUtil.java is at the end of the subtitle IDs, no idea if you want to keep the IDs in order with the UI elements
- same thing with the index for the setting in persistState() inside of PlayerData.java, I added the setting at the end to avoid breaking existing saves
- kept the "subtitle_remember" string in strings.xml as I don't know how to proceed with unused strings. I will be able to add a couple more languages for the new strings in another commit in the future

Thank you for reading and let me know if there are any issues

issues.title: [Feature Request]: Please add a "Chinese (Simplified)" option for online subtitle translation.
[Feature Request]: Languages of preference
issues.body:
### Describe the feature you'd like to request

English is not my language, but it is something I can read (and, without subtitles, I miss most of the videos content, so I do need subtitles, even if they are in English).

Some channels often offers English subtitles others offers english subtitles with another name (I think British English, I couldn't find any differences in the youtube site and I'm far from my TV right now, but the text that appears on the UI is not only "English" is "Something English" or "English Something". 

Also, in the event that no subtitles are available, I use "English (autogenerated)" (which is in a different list than subtitles).

And, of course, if there is a Brazilian Portuguese or even a Portuguese Portuguese subtitle, I take that (*but never for auto generated - they are more useful in english because there are so many errors in the generation that is easier to fix by listening, and the translation now gets in the way)

### Describe the solution you'd like

An option for us to set what languages (**a list of languages**) we understand and that we wish to always use subtitles.

Then, the app would check if

a) The exact match of subtitles are available (for example, "Brazilian Portuguese", or "Portuguese", or "English")
b) No match? Is there another variant of the same language (example: "European English")?
c) Still no match (or no subtitles at all)? Do the same thing for the (autogenerated) languages 

Maybe c) can be another set of options because "English (autogenerated)" are far easier to understand because we're listening to the same language and it's easier to catch the autogeneration errors. In other words: I like subtitles in my language, but I DO NOT use them if it is auto generated.

### Describe alternatives you've considered

There are no alternatives. Every time I need to pause the video, check the "Subtitles" to see if there is some English (sometimes, that other English that is not only "English" doesn't come selected. It seems it searchs for the string "English", no variants). If there is no subtitle available, I have to go back 1 level, then select subtitles (autogenerated) and then search for English.

issue1908Comments.body: The behaviour has changed in the latest update. Clicking the subtitle button will enable or disable the subtitles. Long pressing will open the menu you are already familiar with

> The behaviour has changed in the latest update. Clicking the subtitle button will enable or disable the subtitles. Long pressing will open the menu you are already familiar with

I have just updated to 16.37 but the short click for subtitle disabling doesn't work. It still opens the side menu and interestingly all possible languages are being displayed as subtitle languages regardless of whether there's actually subtitles available for each of them since this update.

Loving SmartTube to bits and was actually waiting for quicker subtitle deactivation so if this would work more reliably in a future version or someone could point me at what I might be doing wrong I'd be grateful!

There are more languages because of the inclusion of auto-translated versions. I haven't looked at the new code so I don't know which subtitle track it's translating from though.

Quick enabling and disabling works for me.

I think the YT web based caption interface is the most efficient.  What's missing here is the automatic selection of the default caption.  E.g, a video has included only one caption, then that caption should be used, instead of the translated caption that's been previously set. I.e, there is a need to separate translated caption from video included caption.  To put it into logic:

If caption is short clicked to enable
      If there is an included caption from the video
             Display included caption
      Else
             If translatable, 
                  If there was one translation selected
                       Display translated caption
                  Else
                       Select translation caption

I'm not sure you understand how this works. The captions are always translated by Google, every video has it. Every subtitle track, whether auto-generated or not, is already translated to all of YouTube's supported languages.

If there is only one subtitle track, then it will be translated to all the various languages, and SmartTubeNext will select your preferred language, as it should (or else how would you read them).

You are correct in that I don't know how behind the scene captions work.  But as a user, I prefer seeing the video's originally included caption. E.g., if I am watching a Chinese language video AND it has a Chinese language caption, I want the Chinese captions displayed instead of English which is what I want translated to when I am viewing other (e.g. Russian) language videos that are translatable.  This is the current capability of the web based YT feature that I get on the Brave Browser.  For example, on the Brave Browser's YT page and viewing this Chinese language video https://youtu.be/c1Mkh_tftrc
The CC button can be turned on or off. When on, the caption displayed is either Chinese, or an Auto Translated Language, all were set by the settings button.   And most importantly, I did not set any preference via the settings button and Chinese was displayed automatically when I enable CC for I think that's the only included caption.  Now if I view another English language video, like https://youtu.be/2aTULNg5F1E
and enable captions, I will see English displayed.  

This is the feature I wish that's available in this app.

I understand now, and it's an easy feature to add, though I wouldn't recommend it as I think YouTube's method of never automatically choosing an auto-translated subtitle ruins the experience. A better method would be to choose a list of languages you understand, and if one of those languages is present in the subtitle track list, to choose that one, and if not, to auto-translate from another language to your most preferred language.

To me the best way would be to choose a priority from a list of languages. Like English, Italian, Danish, French. I don't want to scroll to the infinite list of all the web translated languages like Chinese or Russian which for sure I will never use since I don't speak them. The app should prioritize captions included in the video and only if these are not available, then switch to the translated ones.

I was also thinking about that, scrolling through the whole list is indeed cumbersome. A language list (which is ordered by priority), chooses the subtitle that appears highest in the list, and if none are present, to auto-translate from the existing subtitle track to your most preferred language.

And secondly to add a settings option to disable non-preferred languages from appearing in the auto-translated list (and maybe even a step further, remove human-written subtitles that aren't in your preferred language list).

The new update separates regular subtitles from auto generated ones, though I still do not prefer this. I would rather the app look at my language list (the one in Android Settings) and only show those subtitles (with a checkbox in the SmartTubeNext settings).

I think there are at least 2 main use cases for subtitles: to translate foreign languages, and to aid the hearing-impaired.  But we also have 2 kinds of users, Bilinguals and Monolinguals.  For the Monolinguals, the 2 use cases can be implemented simply as an on/off switch for a previously chosen language.  The original single menu option and the current separation of “Subtitles” and “Subtitles (Auto)” options worked fine, in that the chosen language will be remembered and used when the subtitle switch is turn on.  For the Bilinguals and the hearing-impaired use case, the current separation of options offered slightly improved way of choosing the included subtitle.  But we have to choose each time a different language video is viewed. The Google YouTube app implements perfectly for Bilinguals and the hearing-impaired use case, but suffers from the auto translation use case.  I think the challenge here is to be able to switch to the desired language with just the subtitle on/off switch. 

As for logic, I think we have to have one desired Auto translation language, be that chosen from a list or default to the system language.  We also need to have a subtitle mode: always translate, or always use included subtitle first.  The latter mode will always display the first included subtitle and if none included, do the auto translate.

A couple more items to look into.

1) auto generated subtitles of live video. I don't know how this works in the youtube app, but it will be a nice to have to automatically generate subtitles for live streaming.

2) Auto generated and translated subs don't always work. even with clear audio, there are sections of the video that don't get generated CCs, again, not sure how this works on the original app.
